```{r}
#| label: setup
library(jsonlite)

root <- here::here()
inf <- file.path(root, "artifacts", "inference")
fig <- file.path(inf, "figures")
phdir <- file.path(inf, "ph")
midir <- file.path(inf, "mi")

read_inf <- function(name, sub = NULL) {
  base <- if (is.null(sub)) inf else file.path(inf, sub)
  utils::read.csv(file.path(base, name), check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}

fmt <- function(x, digits = 2) formatC(as.numeric(x), digits = digits, format = "f")
fmt_p <- function(p) {
  p <- as.numeric(p)
  ifelse(p < 0.001, "<0.001", formatC(p, digits = 3, format = "g"))
}

hr_line <- function(row) {
  sprintf(
    "adjusted HR %s (95%% CI %s–%s; nominal p = %s)",
    fmt(row$hr), fmt(row$hr_lcl), fmt(row$hr_ucl), fmt_p(row$p_value)
  )
}

interpret <- function(row, adjustment) {
  direction <- if (as.numeric(row$hr) >= 1) "higher" else "lower"
  interval_note <- if (as.numeric(row$hr_lcl) < 1 && as.numeric(row$hr_ucl) > 1) {
    "The confidence interval was compatible with both a higher and a lower hazard, so the estimate was imprecise."
  } else {
    sprintf("The confidence interval was compatible with a %s hazard of death.", direction)
  }
  sprintf(
    "After adjustment for %s, %s was associated with a %s hazard of death (%s). %s This is a prognostic association, not a causal effect.",
    adjustment,
    row$predictor_label,
    direction,
    hr_line(row),
    interval_note
  )
}

primary <- read_inf("primary_cox_mi.csv")
secondary <- read_inf("secondary_cox_mi.csv")
primary_cc <- read_inf("primary_cox_complete_case.csv")
secondary_cc <- read_inf("secondary_cox_complete_case.csv")
cmp <- read_inf("mi_vs_complete_case.csv")
nl <- read_inf("nonlinear_sensitivity_summary.csv")
phs <- read_inf("ph_diagnostics_summary.csv")
fit <- read_inf("model_fit_summary.csv")
meta <- fromJSON(file.path(inf, "model_metadata.json"))
notes <- fromJSON(file.path(inf, "analysis_notes.json"))
session <- fromJSON(file.path(inf, "r_session_info.json"))
followup <- fromJSON(file.path(root, "artifacts", "descriptive", "followup_summary.json"))
km_os <- fromJSON(file.path(root, "artifacts", "descriptive", "overall_survival_summary.json"))
deviations <- paste(readLines(file.path(root, "docs", "stage6_sap_deviations.md"), warn = FALSE), collapse = "\n")
row_of <- function(tbl, term) tbl[tbl$term == term, ][1, ]
fitv <- function(item) fit$value[fit$item == item]
```

# How to read this report

The **primary clinical model** estimates adjusted associations of age, sex, WBC, and protocol risk group with the hazard of death. The **secondary molecular/cytogenetic model** replaces risk group with mutation and lesion indicators. Hazard ratios and 95% confidence intervals are the main results. Nominal *p*-values and Benjamini–Hochberg *q*-values are reported where they were prespecified; they are not used to add or drop variables.

# Executive summary

- **Population.** Locked primary TARGET-AML overall-survival cohort: **`r meta$cohort_n` analysis persons** younger than 18 years at diagnosis (**`r meta$deaths` deaths**, **`r meta$censored` censored**). Median potential follow-up by reverse Kaplan–Meier was `r sprintf("%.2f", followup$median_followup_years)` years.
- **Primary prognostic variables.** Protocol risk group and log2 white-blood-cell count (WBC), with age and sex as adjustment variables.
- **Strongest / most precisely estimated primary associations.** Both Standard and High risk had substantially higher adjusted hazards than Low risk. High vs Low: `r hr_line(row_of(primary, "risk_group_stdHigh"))`. Standard vs Low: `r hr_line(row_of(primary, "risk_group_stdStandard"))`. WBC per doubling: `r hr_line(row_of(primary, "log2_wbc"))`.
- **Complete-case robustness.** The same formulas were fit on complete cases (primary N = `r primary_cc$n[1]`; secondary N = `r secondary_cc$n[1]`). Direction and magnitude are compared below; complete case is sensitivity, not the primary analysis.
- **Proportional hazards.** Diagnostics used scaled Schoenfeld residuals (`cox.zph`). Remediation, if triggered, followed the prespecified hierarchy and did not replace the primary model (remediation performed: `r isTRUE(meta$ph_remediation_performed)`).
- **Limitations investigators should keep in mind.** This is observational public TARGET data. Missing covariates were handled under a MAR working assumption. Residual confounding remains possible. The 10-year risk set is small. There is no external validation. Language throughout is **prognostic association**, not causal effect.

# 1. Scientific Objective

Among children and adolescents with acute myeloid leukemia in public TARGET-AML data, estimate associations between **prespecified** baseline patient and disease characteristics and the hazard of all-cause death after diagnosis.

The analysis is a prognostic association study. It does not estimate causal effects of intervening on a covariate, protocol, or treatment.

# 2. Prespecified Primary Cohort

The unit of analysis is the **analysis person**. Eligibility was locked before any predictor–survival analysis and was **not** reconstructed in R.

| Item | Frozen value |
| --- | ---: |
| N | `r meta$cohort_n` |
| Deaths | `r meta$deaths` |
| Censored | `r meta$censored` |
| Age at diagnosis | < 18 years |
| Overall 5-year OS | `r sprintf("%.3f", km_os$km_1_3_5_year$survival[3])` |
| Median potential follow-up | `r sprintf("%.2f years (95%% CI %.2f–%.2f)", followup$median_followup_years, followup$median_followup_lcl_years, followup$median_followup_ucl_years)` |

Unknown / Not Reported vital status is not treated as censoring. Predictor completeness does not change cohort membership.

# 3. Prespecified Statistical Models

**Primary clinical model**

```text
`r meta$primary_formula`
```

Tied event times use the **Efron** approximation. Age is linear in `age5` (hazard ratio per 5 years). WBC is linear in `log2_wbc` (hazard ratio per doubling). Sex reference is Female. Risk-group reference is Low. There are **no interaction terms**.

**Secondary molecular/cytogenetic model**

```text
`r meta$secondary_formula`
```

Risk group is **absent**. Primary cytogenetic code and FAB are absent. Binary flags use No as the reference.

These formulas were frozen before any predictor–survival association was examined. Predictors were not added, dropped, or recoded because of *p*-values or hazard ratios.

# 4. Missing Data

Primary missing-data method: **multiple imputation by chained equations** (`mice`), **m = `r meta$m`**, seed **`r meta$seed`**, **`r meta$mice_maxit`** iterations.

Not imputed: analysis-person ID, `os_event`, `os_days`, age, and sex.

Imputation methods followed the freeze: predictive mean matching for `log2_wbc`; polytomous regression for risk group; logistic regression for binary molecular and lesion flags. Auxiliary predictors included marrow and peripheral blasts, CNS (Yes/No), collapsed race, ethnicity, an AML1031 source indicator, `os_event`, and a **nonparametric Nelson–Aalen** cumulative hazard. Post-baseline treatment and response variables were not used.

Unresolved risk-group tokens `10` and `30` (n = 3) remained missing for inference. They were not mapped to Low/Standard/High.

![MICE chain-mean traces](`r file.path(midir, "mi_trace_plots.png")`)

Diagnostics are in `artifacts/inference/mi/`. Completed person-level imputations are gitignored.

# 5. Primary Clinical Model

Pooled using **Rubin's rules on the coefficient (log hazard ratio) scale**. Hazard ratios are exponentiated pooled coefficients. Hazard ratios were not averaged across imputations.

```{r}
#| label: primary-table
knitr::kable(
  primary[, c("predictor_label", "comparison_or_unit", "hr", "hr_lcl", "hr_ucl", "p_value", "fmi")],
  digits = 3,
  col.names = c("Predictor", "Comparison / unit", "HR", "95% CI lower", "95% CI upper", "Nominal p", "FMI"),
  caption = "Primary clinical Cox model, multiply imputed and pooled."
)
```

![Primary clinical model forest plot](`r file.path(fig, "forest_primary_clinical.png")`)

`r interpret(row_of(primary, "age5"), "age, sex, WBC, and risk group")`

`r interpret(row_of(primary, "sex_stdMale"), "age, sex, WBC, and risk group")`

`r interpret(row_of(primary, "log2_wbc"), "age, sex, WBC, and risk group")`

`r interpret(row_of(primary, "risk_group_stdStandard"), "age, sex, WBC, and risk group")`

`r interpret(row_of(primary, "risk_group_stdHigh"), "age, sex, WBC, and risk group")`

Pooled global test for risk group (2 df): `r notes$risk_group_global$method`. Statistic = `r fmt(notes$risk_group_global$statistic, 2)`; p = `r fmt_p(notes$risk_group_global$p_value)`.

Both Standard and High protocol risk groups had substantially higher adjusted hazards than Low risk. The point estimates should not be described as a monotonic Standard < High progression.

Descriptive concordance (mean across imputations): **`r sprintf("%.3f", notes$primary_concordance$mean)`**. This is not a prediction-model validation statistic and was not optimized.

# 6. Secondary Molecular/Cytogenetic Model

Benjamini–Hochberg q-values are reported **only** for the frozen biological family (FLT3/ITD, NPM, CEBPA, t(8;21), inv(16), MLL/KMT2A, monosomy 7). Age, sex, and WBC are adjustment variables and are not in the FDR family.

```{r}
#| label: secondary-table
knitr::kable(
  secondary[, c("predictor_label", "comparison_or_unit", "hr", "hr_lcl", "hr_ucl", "p_value", "q_value")],
  digits = 3,
  col.names = c("Predictor", "Comparison / unit", "HR", "95% CI lower", "95% CI upper", "Nominal p", "BH q"),
  caption = "Secondary molecular/cytogenetic Cox model. q-values apply only to the frozen biological family."
)
```

![Secondary molecular model forest plot](`r file.path(fig, "forest_secondary_molecular.png")`)

```{r}
#| label: secondary-interp
bio <- secondary[!secondary$term %in% c("age5", "sex_stdMale", "log2_wbc"), ]
paragraphs <- vapply(
  seq_len(nrow(bio)),
  function(i) interpret(bio[i, , drop = FALSE], "age, sex, and WBC"),
  character(1)
)
```

`r paste(paragraphs, collapse = "\n\n")`

Descriptive concordance (mean across imputations): **`r sprintf("%.3f", notes$secondary_concordance$mean)`**.

# 7. Complete-Case Sensitivity Analysis

The formulas, references, and transformations were unchanged. Rows with missing model covariates were omitted from that fit only.

| Model | Complete-case N | Deaths | Percent of primary cohort |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Primary clinical | `r primary_cc$n[1]` | `r primary_cc$deaths[1]` | `r primary_cc$percent_of_primary_cohort[1]`% |
| Secondary molecular | `r secondary_cc$n[1]` | `r secondary_cc$deaths[1]` | `r secondary_cc$percent_of_primary_cohort[1]`% |

```{r}
#| label: mi-cc
knitr::kable(
  cmp[, c("model", "predictor_label", "hr_mi", "hr_lcl_mi", "hr_ucl_mi", "hr_cc", "hr_lcl_cc", "hr_ucl_cc", "qualitative")],
  digits = 3,
  col.names = c("Model", "Predictor", "MI HR", "MI LCL", "MI UCL", "CC HR", "CC LCL", "CC UCL", "Qualitative"),
  caption = "Multiply imputed vs complete-case adjusted hazard ratios."
)
```

Qualitative labels compare direction and magnitude. They are not a declaration that one method is correct because its intervals are narrower.

# 8. Functional-Form Sensitivity

Restricted cubic splines used **prespecified knots** (10th, 50th, 90th percentiles from the descriptive analysis). Knots were not moved using AIC, *p*-values, or model results. The primary linear `age5` and log2-linear WBC specifications were **not replaced**.

```{r}
#| label: spline-table
knitr::kable(
  nl,
  digits = 3,
  caption = "Spline overall and nonlinearity tests. Complete-case Wald tests and median tests across imputations."
)
```

Relative-hazard curves use the cohort median as the reference (age `r fmt(nl$reference[1])`; WBC median 26.7 ×10³/mcL). Those references were taken from the descriptive analysis, not chosen after seeing which reference made the figure look strongest.

![Age spline relative hazard](`r file.path(fig, "age_spline_relative_hazard.png")`)

![WBC spline relative hazard](`r file.path(fig, "wbc_spline_relative_hazard.png")`)

# 9. Proportional-Hazards Diagnostics

Assessment used scaled Schoenfeld residuals, covariate-specific tests, a global test, and plots. Classification combined the test, the residual correlation (`rho`), and whether the variable is a nuisance adjustment or a scientifically important predictor. A p-value below 0.05 was not automatically treated as a major violation.

```{r}
#| label: ph-table
knitr::kable(
  phs[, intersect(c("model", "term", "role", "rho", "chisq", "df", "p", "classification", "decision", "mi_median_classification"), names(phs))],
  digits = 3,
  caption = "Complete-case cox.zph diagnostics with prespecified classifications."
)
```

![Primary model Schoenfeld plots](`r file.path(phdir, "primary_cox_zph_complete_case.png")`)

![Secondary model Schoenfeld plots](`r file.path(phdir, "secondary_cox_zph_complete_case.png")`)

Remediation performed: **`r isTRUE(meta$ph_remediation_performed)`**. The original Cox specifications remain the primary results.

# 10. Influence Diagnostics

Deviance residuals, martingale residuals, and dfbeta were examined on complete-case fits. Patient-level lists are gitignored. **No valid participant was deleted because they were influential.**

![Primary deviance residuals](`r file.path(fig, "primary_deviance_residuals.png")`)

![Secondary deviance residuals](`r file.path(fig, "secondary_deviance_residuals.png")`)

# 11. Descriptive Kaplan–Meier Figures

Unadjusted curves were prespecified only for **risk group** and **FLT3/ITD**. Missing values are excluded from each figure. These plots are descriptive and were **not** used for variable selection. Log-rank tests were **not** computed.

![Unadjusted KM by risk group](`r file.path(fig, "km_risk_group.png")`)

![Unadjusted KM by FLT3/ITD](`r file.path(fig, "km_flt3_itd.png")`)

# 12. Interpretation

## Primary clinical findings

Emphasis remains on risk group and WBC, as specified before model fitting. The Standard and High comparisons are each versus Low risk; they are not a ranked dose–response across three ordered categories.

`r interpret(row_of(primary, "risk_group_stdHigh"), "age, sex, and WBC")`

`r interpret(row_of(primary, "risk_group_stdStandard"), "age, sex, and WBC")`

`r interpret(row_of(primary, "log2_wbc"), "age, sex, and risk group")`

Age and sex were estimated as adjustment variables. They are interpreted as prognostic associations, not as targets of intervention.

## Secondary molecular findings

The secondary model asks a different question: granular mutation and lesion indicators **without** protocol risk group, so that overlapping cytogenetic information is not double-counted.

Nominal p-values and BH q-values should be read together. q-values are not a ranking exercise and were not used to drop predictors.

## Robustness

Complete-case and multiply imputed estimates were compared for direction and magnitude. Nonlinear spline sensitivities assess whether linear `age5` and log2-linear WBC are materially inadequate; they do not automatically replace the primary forms. PH diagnostics assess whether reported hazard ratios should be read as average relative hazards over follow-up.

# 13. Limitations

- Observational study of public TARGET-AML data.
- Prognostic associations, not causal effects.
- Multiple integrated open clinical-supplement sources with documented provenance and some source conflicts.
- Missing baseline covariates; multiple imputation relies on a MAR working assumption that the descriptive analysis did not prove. MNAR remains possible.
- Potential residual confounding, including unmeasured disease biology and care access.
- Cox proportional-hazards assumptions; material departures, if classified, were handled as sensitivity analyses rather than silent model replacement.
- Sparse categories exist (for example monosomy 7).
- The 10-year Kaplan–Meier risk set is small (16 persons).
- No external validation and no train/test prediction split. Concordance is descriptive only.

# 15. Conclusions

The analysis executed the prespecified plan on the locked primary cohort. Adjusted associations are reported with hazard ratios and 95% confidence intervals and, for the secondary biological family, BH *q*-values. The primary clinical model remains the primary result. Sensitivity analyses (complete case, splines, and PH remediation if triggered) inform robustness and do not rewrite the prespecified specification.

# 16. Out of scope

This report stops after the prespecified frequentist survival analysis. Bayesian survival models, competing risks, time-dependent treatment effects beyond PH remediation, machine-learning prediction, external validation, and dashboards are outside the scope of this study.
